summary: AttemptRecord's shared O_EXCL '.next' staging file is never cleaned up, so one failed write wedges every later transition, and the intent-failure test masks it by replacing _replace wholesale.
failure_scenario: Disk full (ENOSPC) while writing '<record>.next' during intend(): the O_EXCL-created '.next' remains, intend() returns a refusal, then _settle_attempt's complete('not dispatched', ...) hits FileExistsError on the same '.next', which suppress(OSError) swallows. The durable record stays at phase 'acquired' and never gets its 'not dispatched'/'possibly dispatched' classification. The same leftover blocks any later observe_callbacks or complete.
evidence: Reproduced with a scratch test (not committed): monkeypatch attempt_record.os.write to raise ENOSPC once, then call intend() and complete(). intend() returned 'could not record intent: No space left on device'. The directory held a.attempt and a.attempt.next. complete() raised FileExistsError on a.attempt.next, and a.attempt still read phase 'acquired'. src/constructicon/substrate/executors/attempt_record.py:106-128 and codex.py:1768-1770 (suppress(OSError)). test_an_intent_that_cannot_be_recorded_is_a_refusal_not_a_raise patches record._replace, so it never reaches _write or the O_EXCL staging path. Not determined whether this is introduced or pre-existing.

summary: A provider with egress=None accepts an identity that claims a specific egress-relay policy, and the test pins that mismatch as a successful turn.
failure_scenario: CodexOperatorProvider.__init__ only compares identity.egress digests with the policy when a policy is supplied (codex.py:2348-2353). With egress=None, any egress digests are accepted. test_no_policy_allocates_no_relay_and_mounts_no_leaf builds an identity from policy_for(443) and passes no policy, so the provider is available (unavailable_reasons=()). The sealed revision then names a relay boundary that is never allocated, and the turn is published as success. The 'stronger denial' justification in the class docstring holds for the physical zone, but the published identity no longer describes it (I4).
evidence: Read test_codex_egress.py:256-275 and codex.py:2263-2273, 2340-2395. The test passes unmodified (242 passed in the focused run). The claimed physical 'lo only' denial is not exercised by this scripted launcher, so the impact on the real zone is unverified.

summary: The refusal cases in the reconcile-contradiction test have no match strings, and the second case is refused for a different reason than its comment implies.
failure_scenario: The 'absent resource_ref' row is refused with 'a codex recovery row is not this stale invocation', not as a missing-reference refusal. Any ContractViolation satisfies the test, so a regression that moved the check or dropped the missing-reference guard would still pass.
evidence: Scratch probe printed the reasons: 'a codex recovery reference contradicts its durable row' for the first row and 'a codex recovery row is not this stale invocation' for the second.

summary: The WRITE argument, ninth-effect and no-callback refusal tests assert only ExecutorFailure and no worker call, not the refusal reason or phase.
failure_scenario: Any earlier failure (handshake, framing, budget) also yields ExecutorFailure with calls == [], so the test could pass without reaching the argument or callback-ceiling guard it names. The same applies to the 'legacy' branch of test_eight_full_write_programs_fit_producer_stdout in test_claude_task_budgets.py:102-106.
evidence: Probe output shows today's reasons are correct: known_refusal=mcp-arguments for all four argument shapes, mcp-call for the ninth effect, stream-bound for the legacy budget. None of this is asserted. The refusal detail for the WRITE recipe also reads 'Claude READ refused', which no test pins.

summary: Several assertions are tautologies or can never fail, giving false assurance.
failure_scenario: (a) The loop asserting inspect.getsource(rule) in inspect.getsource(codex) is always true for module-level functions. (b) test_codex_native.py:117-118 asserts each preamble record is not a substring of the fixed '[N records withheld ...]' marker, which holds by construction. (c) test_codex_matrix.py:301-307 compares two runs with identical inputs and an inspect.signature name filter, which cannot show overage independence.
evidence: Read the assertions; no mutation was run against them.

summary: Credential-file shape coverage tests only one wrong mode (0o644), so the exact-0600 rule is not shown to reject other mode variants.
failure_scenario: check_credential requires S_IMODE == 0o600. Untested variants (0o400, 0o700, 0o4600) could regress without a failing test, for example if the check were loosened to '& 0o077 == 0'.
evidence: CREDENTIAL_SHAPES covers absent, world-readable, second-name, other-owner, directory and symlink. Real check_credential runs; only the syscalls are faked (operator_store.py:1065-1080, operator_store_world.py:166-175).

summary: A stale comment says the pre-acceptance read id is 5; FORGED_GOOD_ACCOUNT uses 6 after the spend readbacks were added.
failure_scenario: A maintainer 'fixing' the id to match the comment turns the forged-reply tests into unsolicited-reply tests that still pass for a different reason.
evidence: The EIGHT request order puts the post-turn account/read at id 6. The comment at test_codex_adapter.py:2016 says 5.

summary: test_codex_store: the credential-shape refusals reach the real check_credential/open_credential guard (only syscalls faked), have an accepting twin, and assert the opened descriptor is closed; the retained-lock, closure-race, cancelled-caller fd-ordering and cleanup tests pass and are meaningful.

test_codex_refusal, test_codex_startup, test_codex_spend and test_codex_matrix: account/updated and rate-limit notice allowlists, plan-literal latching, forged and duplicate reply-id handling, and the pre- and post-turn readback gates all have accepting and refusing twins. The accepted-limit behavior that an absent spendControlReached is not 'reached' is documented in spend_faults, so it was not reported.

test_codex_qualification, test_codex_read_stage, test_codex_maintenance_authorization and test_codex_callback_observations: epoch, expiry, run and invocation binding, one-attempt spending, callback-snapshot latching and non-retraction hold. The focused credential-free run of 242 tests passed.
